zouave: (a) One of an active and hardy body of soldiers in the French service, originally Arabs, but now composed of Frenchmen who wear the Arab dress. (b) Hence, one of a body of soldiers who adopt the dress and drill of the Zouaves, as was done by a number of volunteer regiments in the army of the United States in the Civil War, 1861-65.
zooegeny: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
zollverein: Literally, a customs union; specifically, applied to the several customs unions successively formed under the leadership of Prussia among certain German states for establishing liberty of commerce among themselves and common tariff on imports, exports, and transit. Note: In 1834 a zollverein was established which included most of the principal German states except Austria.
zosterops: A genus of birds that comprises the white-eyes. See White-eye.
zorilla: Either one of two species of small African carnivores of the genus Ictonyx allied to the weasels and skunks. [Written also zoril, and zorille.] Note: The best-known species (Ictonyx zorilla) has black shiny fur with white bands and spots. It has anal glands which produce a very offensive secretion, similar to that of the skunk.
zoetrope: An optical toy, in which figures made to revolve on the inside of a cylinder, and viewed through slits in its circumference, appear like a single figure passing through a series of natural motions as if animated or mechanically moved.
zoutch: To stew, as flounders, eels, etc., with just enough or liquid to cover them. Smart.
zoneless: Not having a zone; ungirded. The reeling goddess with the zoneless waist. Cowper. In careless folds, loose fell her zoneless vest. Mason.
zooelogy: 1. That part of biology which relates to the animal kingdom, including the structure, embryology, evolution, classification, habits, and distribution of all animals, both living and extinct. 2. A treatise on this science.
zooephagous: Feeding on animals. Note: This is a more general term than either sarcophagous or carnivorous.
zonaria: A division of Mammalia in which the placenta is zonelike.
zonal: Of or pertaining to a zone; having the form of a zone or zones. Zonal equation (Crystallog.), the mathematical relation which belongs to all the planes of a zone, and expresses their common position with reference to the axes.
zoanthacea: A suborder of Actinaria, including Zoanthus and allied genera, which are permanently attached by their bases.
zoochlorella: One of the small green granulelike bodies found in the interior of certain stentors, hydras, and other invertebrates.
zoographer: One who describes animals, their forms and habits.
zooemelanin: A pigment giving the black color to the feathers of many birds.
zooenite: (a) One of the segments of the body of an articulate animal. (b) One of the theoretic transverse divisions of any segmented animal.
zoospore: 1. (Bot.) A spore provided with one or more slender cilia, by the vibration of which it swims in the water. Zoöspores are produced by many green, and by some olive-brown, algæ. In certain species they are divided into the larger macrozoöspores and the smaller microzoöspores. Called also sporozoid, and swarmspore. 2. (Zoöl.) See Swarmspore.
zooesperm: One of the spermatic particles; spermatozoid.
zoon: (a) An animal which is the sole product of a single egg; -- opposed to zooid. H. Spencer. (b) Any one of the perfectly developed individuals of a compound animal.
zoological: Of or pertaining to zoölogy, or the science of animals.
zooephyte: (a) Any one of numerous species of invertebrate animals which more or less resemble plants in appearance, or mode of growth, as the corals, gorgonians, sea anemones, hydroids, bryozoans, sponges, etc., especially any of those that form compound colonies having a branched or treelike form, as many corals and hydroids. (b) Any one of the Zoöphyta.
zooegrapher: One who describes animals, their forms and habits.
zooephytoid: Pertaining to, or resembling, a zoöphyte.
zonar: A belt or girdle which the Christians and Jews of the Levant were obliged to wear to distinguish them from Mohammedans. [Written also zonnar.]
zoophytoid: Pertaining to, or resembling, a zoöphyte.
zooe: A combining form from Gr. zwo^,n an animal, as in zoögenic, zoölogy, etc.
zoophoric: Bearing or supporting the figure of an animal; as, a zoöphoric column.
zoographic: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
zokor: An Asiatic burrowing rodent (Siphneus aspalax) resembling the mole rat. It is native of the Altai Mountains.
zodiacal: Of or pertaining to the zodiac; situated within the zodiac; as, the zodiacal planets. Zodiacal light, a luminous tract of the sky, of an elongated, triangular figure, lying near the ecliptic, its base being on the horizon, and its apex at varying altitudes. It is to be seen only in the evening, after twilight, and in the morning before dawn.
zooetic: Containing the remains of organized bodies; -- said of rock or soil.
zooegony: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
zooesporic: Of or pertaining to zoöspores; of the nature of zoöspores.
zooegenic: Of or pertaining to zoögeny, animal production.
zoocyst: A cyst formed by certain Protozoa and unicellular plants which the contents divide into a large number of granules, each of which becomes a germ.
zooegloea: A colony or mass of bacteria imbedded in a viscous gelatinous substance. The zoögloea is characteristic of a transitory stage through which rapidly multiplying bacteria pass in the course of their evolution. Also used adjectively.
zoologize: To study zoölogy; esp., to collect animals for study.
zoroastrianism: The religious system of Zoroaster, the legislator and prophet of the ancient Persians, which was the national faith of Persia; mazdeism. The system presupposes a good spirit (Ormuzd) and an opposing evil spirit (Ahriman). Cf. Fire worship, under Fire, and Parsee.
zolaism: The literary theories and practices of the French novelist Emile Zola (1840-1902); naturalism, esp. in a derogatory sense. -- Zo"la*ist, n. -- Zo`la*is"tic (#), a. -- Zo"la*ize (#), v. ZOLLNER'S LINES Zöll"ner's lines`. [So called after Friedrich Zöllner, a German physicist.] Parallel lines that are made to appear convergent or divergent by means of oblique intersections.
zoographical: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
zodiac: 1. (Astron.) (a) An imaginary belt in the heavens, 16º or 18º broad, in the middle of which is the ecliptic, or sun's path. It comprises the twelve constellations, which one constituted, and from which were named, the twelve signs of the zodiac. (b) A figure representing the signs, symbols, and constellations of the zodiac. 2. A girdle; a belt.
zoonomy: The laws animal life, or the science which treats of the phenomena of animal life, their causes and relations.
zooephaga: An artificial group comprising various carnivorous and insectivorous animals.
zoosporic: Of or pertaining to zoöspores; of the nature of zoöspores.
zoophaga: An artificial group comprising various carnivorous and insectivorous animals.
zona: A zone or band; a layer. Zona pellucida. Etym: [NL.] (Biol.) (a) The outer transparent layer, or envelope, of the ovum. It is a more or less elastic membrane with radiating striæ, and corresponds to the cell wall of an ordinary cell. See Ovum, and Illust. of Microscope. (b) The zona radiata.
zoilism: Resemblance to Zoilus in style or manner; carping criticism; detraction. Bring candid eyes the perusal of men's works, and let not Zoilism or detraction blast well-intended labors. Sir T. Browne.
zonate: Divided by parallel planes; as, zonate tetraspores, found in certain red algæ.
zoomorphism: 1. The transformation of men into beasts. Smart. 2. The quality of representing or using animal forms; as, zoömorphism in ornament. 3. The representation of God, or of gods, in the form, or with the attributes, of the lower animals. To avoid the error of anthropomorphism, we fall into the vastly greater, and more absurd, error of zoömorphism. Mivart.
zootic: Containing the remains of organized bodies; -- said of rock or soil.
zoosperm: One of the spermatic particles; spermatozoid.
zooecyst: A cyst formed by certain Protozoa and unicellular plants which the contents divide into a large number of granules, each of which becomes a germ.
zooemorphism: 1. The transformation of men into beasts. Smart. 2. The quality of representing or using animal forms; as, zoömorphism in ornament. 3. The representation of God, or of gods, in the form, or with the attributes, of the lower animals. To avoid the error of anthropomorphism, we fall into the vastly greater, and more absurd, error of zoömorphism. Mivart.
zoroastrian: Of or pertaining to Zoroaster, or his religious system. | A follower of Zoroaster; one who accepts Zoroastrianism.
zoophyta: An extensive artificial and heterogeneous group of animals, formerly adopted by many zoölogists. It included the coelenterates, echinoderms, sponges, Bryozoa, Protozoa, etc. Note: Sometimes the name is restricted to the Coelentera, or to the Anthozoa.
zoanthoid: Of or pertaining to the Zoanthacea.
zoilean: Having the characteristic of Zoilus, a bitter, envious, unjust critic, who lived about 270 years before Christ.
zootomy: The dissection or the anatomy of animals; -- distinguished from androtomy.
zone: 1. A girdle; a cincture. (poetic) An embroidered zone surrounds her waist. Dryden. Loose were her tresses seen, her zone unbound. Collins. 2. (Geog.) One of the five great divisions of the earth,… | To girdle; to encircle. Keats.
zooenomy: The laws animal life, or the science which treats of the phenomena of animal life, their causes and relations.
zootrophic: Of or pertaining to the nourishment of animals.
zooechemistry: Animal chemistry; particularly, the description of the chemical compounds entering into the composition of the animal body, in distinction from biochemistry.
zoochemistry: Animal chemistry; particularly, the description of the chemical compounds entering into the composition of the animal body, in distinction from biochemistry.
zoology: 1. That part of biology which relates to the animal kingdom, including the structure, embryology, evolution, classification, habits, and distribution of all animals, both living and extinct. 2. A treatise on this science.
zooephoric: Bearing or supporting the figure of an animal; as, a zoöphoric column.
zooedendrium: The branched, and often treelike, support of the colonies of certain Infusoria.
zooelogist: One who is well versed in zoölogy.
zopilote: The urubu, or American black vulture.
zooephytological: Of or pertaining to zoöphytology; as, zoöphytological observations.
zooelogical: Of or pertaining to zoölogy, or the science of animals.
zooepraxiscope: An instrument similar to, or the same as, the, the phenakistoscope, by means of which pictures projected upon a screen are made to exhibit the natural movements of animals, and the like.
zoo: A combining form from Gr. zwo^,n an animal, as in zoögenic, zoölogy, etc.
zoomelanin: A pigment giving the black color to the feathers of many birds.
zoophagan: A animal that feeds on animal food.
zooetomist: One who dissects animals, or is skilled in zoötomy.
zooen: (a) An animal which is the sole product of a single egg; -- opposed to zooid. H. Spencer. (b) Any one of the perfectly developed individuals of a compound animal.
zoophorous: The part between the architrave and cornice; the frieze; -- so called from the figures of animals carved upon it.
zostera: A genus of plants of the Naiadaceæ, or Pondweed family. Zostera marina is commonly known as sea wrack, and eelgrass.
zooetomy: The dissection or the anatomy of animals; -- distinguished from androtomy.
zoologist: One who is well versed in zoölogy.
zoanthropy: A kind of monomania in which the patient believes himself transformed into one of the lower animals.
zoanthus: A genus of Actinaria, including numerous species, found mostly in tropical seas. The zooids or polyps resemble small, elongated actinias united together at their bases by fleshy stolons, and thus forming extensive groups. The tentacles are small and bright colored.
zoanthodeme: The zooids of a compound anthozoan, collectively.
zoophagous: Feeding on animals. Note: This is a more general term than either sarcophagous or carnivorous.
zoned: 1. Wearing a zone, or girdle. Pope. 2. Having zones, or concentric bands; striped. 3. (Bot.) Zonate.
zoosporangium: A spore, or conceptacle containing zoöspores.
zoonite: (a) One of the segments of the body of an articulate animal. (b) One of the theoretic transverse divisions of any segmented animal.
zoopraxiscope: An instrument similar to, or the same as, the, the phenakistoscope, by means of which pictures projected upon a screen are made to exhibit the natural movements of animals, and the like.
zooechlorella: One of the small green granulelike bodies found in the interior of certain stentors, hydras, and other invertebrates.
zooecytium: The common support, often branched, of certain species of social Infusoria.
zoogony: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
zooegraphical: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
zoea: A peculiar larval stage of certain decapod Crustacea, especially of crabs and certain Anomura. [Written also zoæa.] Note: In this stage the anterior part of the body is relatively large, and usually bears three or four long spines. The years are conspicuous, and the antennæ and jaws are long, fringed organs used in swimming.
zooephagan: A animal that feeds on animal food.
zoocytium: The common support, often branched, of certain species of social Infusoria.
zooespore: 1. (Bot.) A spore provided with one or more slender cilia, by the vibration of which it swims in the water. Zoöspores are produced by many green, and by some olive-brown, algæ. In certain species they are divided into the larger macrozoöspores and the smaller microzoöspores. Called also sporozoid, and swarmspore. 2. (Zoöl.) See Swarmspore.
zoonic: Of or pertaining to animals; obtained from animal substances.
zoism: 1. Reverence for animal life or belief in animal powers and influences, as among savages. 2. (Biol.) A doctrine, now discarded, that the phenomena of life are due to a peculiar vital principle; the theory of vital force.
zonure: Any one of several of South African lizards of the genus Zonura, common in rocky situations.
zoodendrium: The branched, and often treelike, support of the colonies of certain Infusoria.
zooidal: Of or pertaining to a zooid; as, a zooidal form.
zooegeography: The study or description of the geographical distribution of animals.
zoantharian: Of or pertaining to the Zoantharia. -- n. One of the Anthozoa.
zooesporangium: A spore, or conceptacle containing zoöspores.
zootomist: One who dissects animals, or is skilled in zoötomy.
zooetrophic: Of or pertaining to the nourishment of animals.
zooeerythrine: A peculiar organic red coloring matter found in the feathers of various birds.
zooegraphic: Of or pertaining to the description of animals.
zobo: A kind of domestic cattle reared in Asia for its flesh and milk. It is supposed to be a hybrid between the zebu and the yak.
zonular: Of or pertaining to a zone; zone-shaped. "The zonular type of a placenta." Dana.
zohar: A Jewish cabalistic book attributed by tradition to Rabbi Simon ben Yochi, who lived about the end of the 1st century, a. d. Modern critics believe it to be a compilation of the 13th century. Encyc. Brit.
zolaesque: In the style of Zola (see Zolaism).
zounds: An exclamation formerly used as an oath, and an expression of anger or wonder.
zoogenic: Of or pertaining to zoögeny, animal production.
zoic: Of or pertaining to animals, or animal life.
zooephyta: An extensive artificial and heterogeneous group of animals, formerly adopted by many zoölogists. It included the coelenterates, echinoderms, sponges, Bryozoa, Protozoa, etc. Note: Sometimes the name is restricted to the Coelentera, or to the Anthozoa.
zoophyte: (a) Any one of numerous species of invertebrate animals which more or less resemble plants in appearance, or mode of growth, as the corals, gorgonians, sea anemones, hydroids, bryozoans, sponges, etc., especially any of those that form compound colonies having a branched or treelike form, as many corals and hydroids. (b) Any one of the Zoöphyta.
zooegraphy: A description of animals, their forms and habits.
zooephorous: The part between the architrave and cornice; the frieze; -- so called from the figures of animals carved upon it.
zooecium: One of the cells or tubes which inclose the feeling zooids of Bryozoa. See Illust. of Sea Moss.
zoophytological: Of or pertaining to zoöphytology; as, zoöphytological observations.
zoography: A description of animals, their forms and habits.
zooelogically: In a zoölogical manner; according to the principles of zoölogy.
zoogloea: A colony or mass of bacteria imbedded in a viscous gelatinous substance. The zoögloea is characteristic of a transitory stage through which rapidly multiplying bacteria pass in the course of their evolution. Also used adjectively.
zooerythrine: A peculiar organic red coloring matter found in the feathers of various birds.
zoogeography: The study or description of the geographical distribution of animals.
zoogeny: The doctrine of the formation of living beings.
zooid: Pertaining to, or resembling, an animal. | 1. (Biol.) An organic body or cell having locomotion, as a spermatic cell or spermatozooid. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) An animal in one of its inferior stages of development, as one of the intermediate forms in…
zooenic: Of or pertaining to animals; obtained from animal substances.
zoisite: A grayish or whitish mineral occurring in orthorhombic, prismatic crystals, also in columnar masses. It is a silicate of alumina and lime, and is allied to epidote.
zoologically: In a zoölogical manner; according to the principles of zoölogy.
